name: Replicating Momentum
description: Reproduce the momentum effect from the original paper and test it on later data.

lessonObjectives.l1-reading-a-paper: Read a paper’s abstract, data section and main table in that order.
lessonObjectives.l2-jt-design: Describe the formation and holding periods behind momentum.
lessonObjectives.l3-main-table: Say what each cell of the main table measures.
lessonObjectives.l4-what-to-replicate: Decide exactly which numbers you will reproduce.
lessonObjectives.l5-replication-plan: Write a plan with data, steps and checks before any code.
lessonObjectives.l6-data-you-can-get: Choose a free data source and note how it differs from the paper’s.
lessonObjectives.l7-winners-and-losers: Rank stocks by past return and form decile portfolios.
lessonObjectives.l9-skip-month: Apply the skip month and see why it matters.
lessonObjectives.l10-matching-the-table: Compare your numbers with the paper’s and explain the gaps.
lessonObjectives.l11-overlapping-errors: Use Newey-West standard errors for overlapping returns.
lessonObjectives.l12-adjusting-for-risk: Regress momentum returns on factor returns.
lessonObjectives.l13-after-publication: Extend the test to data from after the paper.
lessonObjectives.l14-crashes: Study momentum’s worst months and when they happen.
lessonObjectives.l15-replication-note: Write a plain note on how much of the effect survived.
